input.question: Why can’t we hear anything when we are asleep but can wake up to an alarm or a loud enough noise?
input.ground_truth: Your ears are still receiving the sound, but the auditory cortex in your brain chooses to ignore it, otherwise your sleep would be disrupted multiple times every night. It’s not actually just the volume that triggers you to wake up. It’s whether your unconscious mind interprets that sound as a potential threat, for example if your bedroom door opens quietly it could certainly wake you up if you don’t expect anyone to enter your room. Your brain, without you being consciously aware of it, thinks, “that sounds like it could be a threat. I better wake up and check it out.” A loud or abrupt sound will startle you and trigger your fight or flight response, shocking you into consciousness in the same way.

Question: Why can’t we hear anything when we are asleep but can wake up to an alarm or a loud enough noise?

Answer:

response.prediction: When you are asleep, your brain is resting and doesn’t pay attention to most sounds, like someone talking softly or the TV. But if a sound is really loud, like an alarm or a big crash, your brain wakes up because it thinks something important or dangerous is happening. That’s why you can wake up to a loud noise even when you can’t hear quieter sounds while you’re sleeping.
